record.paper_title: Traces on Operator Ideals Defined over the Class of all Banach Spaces and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Few approximable operators despite unconditional structure.
record.original_question: Find Banach spaces that contain an unconditional basic sequence but nevertheless have few approximable operators, meaning that their set app(X) of approximation-number profiles of approximable operators is strictly smaller than the full cone c_0^*(N).

evidence.quote:
Problem 22. Find Banach spaces with an unconditional basic sequence that
have few approximable operators.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. For a bounded linear operator $T: X \to X$, the $n$-th approximation number is
$$a_n(T) = \inf\{\|T - F\| : F: X \to X \text{ bounded linear with } \mathrm{rank}(F) < n\}, \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}.$$
An operator $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ is called approximable if it lies in the operator-norm closure of the finite-rank operators on $X$; equivalently, $a_n(T) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Define
$$\mathrm{app}(X) = \{(a_n(T))_{n \in \mathbb{N}} : T \in \mathcal{L}(X), \ T \text{ approximable}\} \subseteq c_0^*(\mathbb{N}),$$
where $c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$ denotes the cone of non-increasing null sequences of non-negative real numbers. One says that $X$ has few approximable operators if $\mathrm{app}(X) \subsetneq c_0^*(\mathbb{N})$, i.e., there exists a non-increasing null sequence of non-negative reals that is not the approximation-number sequence of any approximable operator on $X$.

Problem: Exhibit a Banach space $X$ that contains an unconditional basic sequence and at the same time has few approximable operators in the sense above.
